answer: Sealed lineage receipts. Each agent operation emits a receipt carrying a hidden opal tag derived from its full ancestry chain. Receipts from two agents that harbor a shared ancestor will, when combined by any verifier, refract through a fixed prism function into an identical output, exposing the fork. An attacker cloning an agent must therefore regenerate a wholly disjoint ancestry for every copy, paying full registration and re-derivation cost per clone rather than copying credentials once. Duplication becomes detectable by anyone holding both receipts.
